name: Deskhand
positioning: A fictional AI support agent that drafts replies to customer tickets and links every claim to the order or help article it came from.
audience: Support leads at online shops with one to ten agents, who need to trust a reply before it goes out.
voice: Plain and specific: order numbers, amounts, dates
Calm about limits: says what it will not do

direction.tier: Product-as-hero with one show-piece: a tilted live console that plays one ticket on load, then a pinned 'exploded reply' where source documents slide out and highlighter lines link each claim to its line. Palette measured against Fin, Sierra, Clay, Ramp and Resend (2026-09-23): light paper, black ink, highlighter yellow as big fields.
devices: Highlighter: yellow marks a claim and the source line it came from, and floods the trial band
Source lines: a connector draws from each citation to its line in the source document
invariants: Header with the Start trial action
Geist for display and text, Geist Mono only for ticket, order and money data
One sample ticket (#2291, cracked lamp, $84 refund) runs through the whole page
Accent only on citations, their sources and the primary action
variables: Which console state a section shows
The refund limit in the limits demo

imagery.subject: The Deskhand console working one ticket: the customer message, the sources it read, the drafted reply and the approval bar
imagery.materials: White paper documents with soft shadows, hairline rules, monospace data, highlighter marks
imagery.lighting: No photography; depth from panel elevation and a soft top-edge highlight
imagery.palette: Off-white paper #f6f6f3, black ink #101114, highlighter yellow #ffe14d as marks and whole fields
invariants: The same ticket, order and customer on every console view
Real-looking but fictional data, labelled in the footer
Citations numbered the same way in every view
avoid: Invented metrics, customer logos or testimonials

motion.character: Opening: headline rises, a highlighter stroke sweeps under the supporting line, the tilted console rises and flattens as you scroll while the agent works ticket #2291. Set-piece: pinned for three screens, three source documents slide out from behind the reply, the reply writes itself with scroll and each citation draws a line to its source. Limits: tickets move between lanes as the slider moves.
motion.reducedMotion: Every console shows its final state; steps stack in normal flow with no pinning.

chapters.question: What is this?
chapters.message: Deskhand drafts replies to support tickets and links each one to its sources.
chapters.visual: Console playing ticket #2291 from arrival to the approval bar.
chapters.transition: Plays once on load; the visitor can approve the refund.
chapters.mobileFallback: Console below the copy, ticket list hidden.

chapters.question: How does it get to a reply?
chapters.message: It reads the order, the help article and the thread, writes a cited reply, then asks before a refund over your limit.
chapters.visual: Pinned exploded view: reply card in the centre, three source documents around it, connector lines.
chapters.transition: Scroll scrubs documents out, words in, highlights and lines, then the approval bar.
chapters.mobileFallback: Reply card then the three documents stacked, final state, no lines.

chapters.question: What does it send without me?
chapters.message: You set a refund limit; tickets above it wait for you, and chargebacks always go to a person.
chapters.visual: Refund slider over two lanes of sample tickets.
chapters.transition: Tickets slide between lanes as the limit changes.

chapters.question: What does it cost?
chapters.message: Free for 14 days, then a price per reply Deskhand sends.
